projects.org: Bangalore Bullsharks (2025), now The Orcas (2026). One team, same members. Self-funded and student-run.
projects.role: CTO & Arm Design Lead (2026) · Software Lead (2025)
projects.result: India national champions in 2025 and 2026, and the only team of ~120 to receive the Sharkpedo Legacy Award at the 2026 World Championship.
bullets: **2025:** No prior competition experience. Our first two ROVs, Leviathan Mark 1 (India nationals) and Leviathan Mark 2 (Worlds), were built for under $2,000 combined. We won India nationals, then competed at the World Championship in Alpena, Michigan, USA as the first Indian team in the Ranger class. Judges awarded us the US Navy Challenge Coin (~4 of ~120 teams). We placed 36th.

**2026:** We built The Orca in about two months for ~$600, against rival budgets of $15,000–20,000. India national champions with a national-record 280/375 points. At the World Championship in Canada, we were the only team of ~120 to receive the Sharkpedo Legacy Award.
As Arm Design Lead, I designed the manipulator arm. The Orca competed with a single-motor gripper.

projects.title: BLADE: Botanical Leaf Analysis & Disease Evaluator
projects.result: A handheld, fully offline crop-disease scanner. Paper under review.
bullets: Built on a Raspberry Pi 4B with a 5 MP camera, a touchscreen interface and a custom 3D-printed enclosure. A pretrained MobileNetV2 convolutional neural network classifies a leaf photo into 38 classes (26 diseases, 12 healthy states) across 14 crops.

The pipeline runs input checks, combines five augmented views of each image (test-time augmentation) and applies confidence thresholds, so the device answers "uncertain" rather than giving a wrong diagnosis.
I rebuilt the device (camera swap, reworked internal layout, full software audit, Git version control, speed optimization) and redesigned the study as a controlled experiment.

**Research question:** why do plant-disease models that score ~99% on lab images fail in real fields? Is the cause the leaf or the background? BLADE photographs the same leaves while changing one condition at a time (background, framing, lighting), which turns a correlation found in earlier studies into a controlled test.
